correctness.rationale: Uniformity of the torus shift and the bound on radius restrict all included lattice points to the four fundamental-square corners. The sum-of-squared-distances identity forces any diagonal pair to accompany a third point. Therefore hull area is half the sum of two opposite-pair indicators. The lens event and the fourfold event have explicit closed elementary intersection areas, deriving every probability and moment. Near onset, diagonal lenses scale as delta to power three halves, while the all-four event scales as a two-dimensional diamond at delta squared. The exact proof is independent of numerical checks.

value.rationale: The disk radii between the square diagonal covering threshold and the next unit-lattice-point threshold form a canonical complete regime, not an arbitrary narrow slice. Exact classification of the area law yields all moments, the two-dimensional perimeter law, and sharp separate exponents for the birth of triangular versus quadrilateral digitized convex hulls. These are natural geometric statistics not determined by the earlier asymptotic integer-hull bounds or counts of distinct digitizations.
